binding_resolver_inverted.vector: the report admits WorldForge resolved the subject

binding_substituted_anchor_actor.vector: WorldForge surveyed a different actor than the one named and reported success

binding_substituted_map.vector: right subject id, wrong level — still not the survey that was asked for

binding_transform_beyond_tolerance.vector: anchor drift of ~1.56cm Euclidean — under 1cm on every single axis, and still outside the L2 tolerance. The per-axis reading of this rail is the trap this fixture exists to catch

binding_wrong_subject_id.vector: a real survey of the wrong subject, returned against this request

report_clean_without_evidence.vector: a clean pass with no evidence behind it

report_dry_probe_claims_runtime.vector: a report that never executed claiming live runtime truth

report_executed_without_observed_anchor.vector: an executed run that cannot say where it actually looked

report_pre_wave1_scratch_shape.vector: the pre-Wave-1 report shape, which predates subject binding entirely and would silently satisfy a gate that only asked whether a report exists

report_resolver_inverted.vector: a report asserting WorldForge chose the subject

report_unknown_failure_code.vector: a failure code invented to look rigorous

report_valid_exceeds_total.vector: more valid samples than were ever taken

report_zero_support_samples_passed.vector: a pass built on zero probed support samples

subject_both_anchor_channels.vector: both anchor channels populated — WorldForge would have to pick one

subject_empty_subject_id.vector: a blank subject id — nothing to bind a report back to

subject_missing_anchor_mode.vector: a subject that never says how its anchor is expressed

subject_missing_map.vector: a subject with no map — WorldForge would have to choose the level

subject_neither_anchor_channel.vector: neither anchor channel populated — the caller never resolved the subject

subject_resolved_by_worldforge.vector: a subject WorldForge claims to have resolved itself — the exact authority inversion v2.6 exists to refuse

subject_unknown_key.vector: an extra key smuggled onto the subject

subject_wrong_schema_version.vector: a subject claiming a schema version this build does not implement

not_yet_testable.nondeterministic_repeated_reports: requires two real editor runs; determinism is enforced at runtime from per_run_hashes, which no static fixture can produce honestly
not_yet_testable.package_dirty_after_cleanup: package_dirty_before / package_dirty_after are not observed or emitted
not_yet_testable.request_hash_mismatch: the runtime report does not yet emit request_hash; there is nothing to mismatch against
not_yet_testable.runtime_report_copied_from_another_reque: replay detection needs request_hash in the report; without it the copy is indistinguishable from a legitimate re-run
not_yet_testable.screenshot_without_runtime_evidence: no screenshot artifact is produced at all under the current -nullrhi pass, so the vector has no on-disk form yet
not_yet_testable.subject_binding_hash_mismatch: the runtime report does not yet emit subject_binding_hash
not_yet_testable.temporary_markers_left_behind: temporary_actor_count_* are not emitted; markers are trace-probed rather than spawned, so there is no count to leave dirty
not_yet_testable.wrong_target_commit: target_commit is never compared; only a 40-hex shape check exists, and only on the live bridge path
not_yet_testable.wrong_target_repository: the scene-survey path does not yet compare resolved_target_repository against the request (the live bridge gate does, the survey gate does not)

note: Fixtures carry no harness metadata on purpose: an embedded _expected_code key would itself be rejected by the strict unknown-key rail, which looks green and proves nothing.
